title: Boss: the mutation gate failed
summary: A pull request is blocked by Stryker's break threshold. Read the report, kill the survivors in the refund policy, then in paging arithmetic and a promotion window.

steps.title: PR #902 is blocked
body: The pipeline ran `dotnet stryker --since:main --break-at 80` on your pull request. Its summary:
All mutants have been tested, and your mutation score has been calculated
│ File               │  % score │ # killed │ # timeout │ # survived │ # no cov │
Final mutation score of 43.75 is below the break threshold of 80
Coverage on all three files is 100%. The report's survivors for `RefundPolicy.cs`:
Treat every survivor as a question: *which behaviour does no test check?* Then write the one precise test that answers it.

code: public static decimal Refund(decimal price, int daysSincePurchase, bool opened, bool damaged)

mutants.name: Equality
mutants.hint: A price of exactly 0 must throw.

mutants.name: Equality
mutants.hint: Day 30 is still inside the window.

mutants.name: Constant
mutants.hint: Assert the exact amount for an opened item.

steps.title: Kill the refund survivors
prompt: public static decimal Refund(decimal price, int daysSincePurchase, bool opened, bool damaged)
if (damaged) return price;                       // damaged: always a full refund, any day
if (daysSincePurchase > 30) return 0m;           // 30 days to change your mind
if (opened) return Math.Round(price * 0.85m, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero);   // 15% restocking fee
The starter holds the PR's current tests (score 50%). Make `RefundTests` kill all **six** planted bugs, including the three survivors from the report.
starter: [Fact] public void Negative_price_throws() => Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(() => RefundPolicy.Refund(-1m, 1, false, false));
[Fact] public void Damaged_items_are_refunded() => Assert.Equal(40m, RefundPolicy.Refund(40m, 60, true, true));
[Fact] public void Opened_items_cost_a_fee() => Assert.True(RefundPolicy.Refund(40m, 3, true, false) < 40m);
[Fact] public void Late_returns_get_nothing() => Assert.Equal(0m, RefundPolicy.Refund(40m, 45, false, false));
solution: public void Price_must_be_positive(int price) => Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>(() => RefundPolicy.Refund(price, 1, false, false));
[Fact] public void Damaged_items_are_refunded_even_when_late() => Assert.Equal(40m, RefundPolicy.Refund(40m, 60, true, true));
[Fact] public void Opened_items_cost_fifteen_percent() => Assert.Equal(34m, RefundPolicy.Refund(40m, 3, true, false));
[Fact] public void Day_30_is_still_refunded() => Assert.Equal(40m, RefundPolicy.Refund(40m, 30, false, false));
[Fact] public void Day_31_gets_nothing() => Assert.Equal(0m, RefundPolicy.Refund(40m, 31, false, false));
[Fact] public void Unopened_items_get_the_full_price() => Assert.Equal(40m, RefundPolicy.Refund(40m, 3, false, false));

target: public static decimal Refund(decimal price, int daysSincePurchase, bool opened, bool damaged)

mutants.name: damaged items follow the 30-day rule
mutants.hint: A damaged item returned after 60 days still gets the full price.

mutants.name: opened items are refunded in full

hints: The report names the three survivors: a price of exactly 0, day 30 itself, and the exact 15% fee.
`Refund(40m, 3, true, false)` is exactly 34.00; `Refund(40m, 30, false, false)` is 40.
Keep the damaged-after-60-days test: it is what stops someone from moving the damaged check below the 30-day rule.
steps.explain: Three tests turned the score from 50% to 100%, and each one names a rule finance would recognise. That is the right way to satisfy a mutation gate: not more tests, sharper ones.

steps.title: Kill the arithmetic survivors in paging
prompt: The API's paging helpers, compiled beside your tests:
public static int PageCount(int totalItems, int pageSize)
public static (int Skip, int Take) Window(int page, int pageSize) => ((page - 1) * pageSize, pageSize);
Write `public class PagingTests` with at least **6** tests. Six planted bugs: Stryker's arithmetic mutations and two removed guards.
solution: public void Page_count_rounds_up(int total, int size, int expected) => Assert.Equal(expected, Paging.PageCount(total, size));
public void Window_skips_the_earlier_pages(int page, int size, int skip) => Assert.Equal((skip, size), Paging.Window(page, size));

target: public static int PageCount(int totalItems, int pageSize)
public static (int Skip, int Take) Window(int page, int pageSize) => ((page - 1) * pageSize, pageSize);

mutants.name: Arithmetic: + pageSize + 1
mutants.hint: 10 items in pages of 5 is 2 pages, not 3.

mutants.name: Arithmetic: no rounding up
mutants.hint: 11 items in pages of 5 is 3 pages.

mutants.name: a page size of 0 is not refused
a negative total is not refused

hints: Rounding up has two edges: an exact multiple (10 in pages of 5) and one more (11).
Without the guard, a page size of 0 throws `DivideByZeroException`, which `Assert.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>` treats as a failure.
steps.explain: Arithmetic mutants die at the edges of integer division and at the first page. Note the guard tests: `Assert.Throws` is exact about the type, so a `DivideByZeroException` does not pass for an argument check.

steps.title: Kill the relational survivors in the promotion window
prompt: Promotions run from a start day to an end day, both included:
public static bool IsValid(DateOnly today, DateOnly starts, DateOnly ends)
if (ends < starts) throw new ArgumentException("A promotion cannot end before it starts.");
Write `public class PromoTests` with at least **5** tests. Five planted bugs. A one-day promotion (`starts == ends`) is allowed.
starter: static readonly DateOnly Starts = new(2026, 11, 27), Ends = new(2026, 11, 30);
[Fact] public void Valid_in_the_middle() => Assert.True(Promo.IsValid(new(2026, 11, 28), Starts, Ends));
solution: static readonly DateOnly Starts = new(2026, 11, 27), Ends = new(2026, 11, 30);
[Fact] public void Valid_on_the_first_day() => Assert.True(Promo.IsValid(Starts, Starts, Ends));
[Fact] public void Valid_on_the_last_day() => Assert.True(Promo.IsValid(Ends, Starts, Ends));
[Fact] public void A_one_day_promotion_is_allowed() => Assert.True(Promo.IsValid(Starts, Starts, Starts));
[Fact] public void Ending_before_starting_is_refused() => Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => Promo.IsValid(Starts, Ends, Starts));

target: public static bool IsValid(DateOnly today, DateOnly starts, DateOnly ends)
if (ends < starts) throw new ArgumentException("A promotion cannot end before it starts.");

mutants.name: a backwards window is accepted
replace: if (ends < starts) throw new ArgumentException("A promotion cannot end before it starts.");

hints: Two inclusive edges, so four tests: on each edge, and one day outside each.
`||` instead of `&&` is true for every day before the end and every day after the start: a day outside the window kills it.
Add the one-day promotion (`Promo.IsValid(day, day, day)` is true) and the backwards window that throws.
steps.explain: Inclusive ranges are where relational mutants live. Four edge tests plus the configuration rules took the file to 100% without a single redundant test.
